solution.solution: An overnight plugin, which rn uses, that starts a night's batch in its own process, at once or, where given a time such as `overnight --at 23:00 2 <worktree>...`, after waiting until that time: it takes rn's works from a queue, each a run of rn in its worktree, and runs up to the given number at once, each by `claude -p --session-id <uuid>`; on success it starts the next; on a non-zero exit it waits and resumes the same session by `claude -p --resume <uuid>` with a prompt to go on, on the work's own model, the wait starting at 5 minutes and doubling to a cap of 60 minutes, and it gives the work up after 6 hours of waiting in all; a record keeps, for each work, its session id, when it failed, when and how often it resumed, and its last result, for the morning; where a run comes to a point that is the user's to decide, it stops there and leaves the point as a question for the morning.
solution.why: A plain retry from outside rests on no wording or output form of Claude Code's, which claude-ac's parse of `resets at HH:MM` already failed to keep up with, and the resume itself shows whether the limit has lifted, so no separate check or watcher is needed; it is a few lines of the plugin's own, so no other author's code with an unclear license runs, and unsnooze and the others do more than this need.

assumption.assumption: A run of rn in `claude -p` that meets the usage limit exits non-zero, and `claude -p --resume <uuid>` after the limit lifts goes on in the same session from where it stopped, with no permission prompt stopping it and no one there, so that by morning each work has reached its end or a question for the user.
assumption.test: On the user's machine, queue a real run of rn with the overnight plugin at night and leave it until it meets the usage limit; in the morning, check in the record that the work failed, resumed after the limit lifted, and reached its end or a question, and that the session's history goes on from where it stopped.

decisions.decision: The run is for a user who instructs an AI and leaves the AI to arrange the work, as the user answered 「ユーザーがAIに指示してAIが段取る」.
Once the limit lifts, the stopped work goes on from where it stopped, and a record remains of what stopped and what resumed, as the user answered 「１と２」.
The aim is that work moves on while the user sleeps and in the morning they only check the results, as the user answered 「１」.
Making the stopped work go on from where it stopped is also to show in the morning what stopped and what resumed, as the user asked 「１やったら２やることにならないの？」 and called the opposite 「そんなおかしな話ある？」.

rn stays a tool the user works with in conversation, and the night's work is a batch in a separate process that rn starts, as the user said 「rnは対話で作業する前提だよね」, 「rnからオーバーナイトを使うようなイメージ」, and 「別プロセスで夜に作業するバッチのようなイメージ」.
The resume relies on an outside watcher, not on Claude Code's `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, as the user answered 「autoContinueAtUsageLimitはあてにならない」 and 「２かな」.
Whether the limit has lifted is found by trying from outside, not by reading Claude Code's messages or output, as the user said 「ごく小さな問い合わせで確かめる これが一番確実でお手軽では？」 and 「人が外からやるならこうなるよね？時間見えてなければ」.

The batch starts works from a queue up to a given parallel count, and on an error it starts the resume again at a growing interval up to a set number of times, as a plain retry, as the user said 「キューから指定された並行数起動 エラーコードが帰ってきたら一定間隔で、再開してを起動するだけでいいのでは？ つまり普通のリトライだよね？その間隔を指数関数じゃないけど、伸ばして何回までとか？」.
The retry runs on the work's own model, not on Haiku, since limits are kept per model too, as the user answered 「１で」.
The wait before each resume starts at 5 minutes and doubles to a cap of 60 minutes, and a work is given up after 6 hours of waiting in all, as the user answered 「1で」.

`overnight` can take a start time, such as `overnight --at 23:00 2 <worktree>...`, so that the AI asked before bed starts the batch at that time, such as when the usage window comes back, with only a wait until that time added before the start, as the user asked 「開始時刻は指定できるの？」 and answered 「１」.
Each work in the queue is a run of rn in its own worktree, since the night's batch is one that rn starts and rn's work lives one run to a worktree.

A night's batch stops at each point that is the user's to decide and leaves it as a question for the morning, since rn asks the user what is theirs and fills no gap by guessing, and no one answers at night.
The talk is in Japanese, the language of the user's words, and the deliverables are in English, the language of the repository's documents, so each reader reads their own.

Step 1 is good once its logic is shown working, by unit tests in which stand-ins take the place of `claude`, `sleep`, and the clock, with no run on the real Claude Code needed for it, as the user said 「ロジックが動いていればOKです」 and 「モックでロジックをすべてテストできるよね？」.

`overnight` is written in Python, its command `bin/overnight` only starting it, with unit tests that run every line and branch of it, a README, and a CHANGELOG, since `.claude/rules/dev.md` asks every plugin of ccpm for "the LICENSE, README, CHANGELOG, and unit tests that any plugin of ccpm carries", and `dev/README.md` says CI checks "each plugin's unit tests, and that they run every line and branch of the plugins' code", which `pyproject.toml` measures on `*.py` files only.

The specification of overnight.py, in its module opening and main's interface, states that every run of `claude` carries the night's prompt to stop at each point that is the user's and leave it as a question for the morning, that a resume asks the session to go on from where it stopped, and that an error a work meets stops the batch: from that moment no work not yet started starts, each started work runs to its end, the record notes each work that never started, and the batch ends with the error's trace in batch.log and no end noted, and the code does just that, since the solution asks for the first two, the third is how the morning shows why a batch stopped and which queued works never ran, which the record now leaves out and timing now decides, and a maintainer who can't trace a behavior to a case can't tell whether to keep it.

The tests of overnight meet `claude` only as a stand-in executable on the PATH and start the batch only through `main`, as overnight's callers do, check the whole record and the whole session log of each case, and give each refusal its own named test, a digit that isn't ASCII, such as `²`, included, so that a change in how overnight runs `claude` keeps them passing where no behavior changed, and a dropped behavior or refusal fails them, within the user's stand-ins for `claude`, `sleep`, and the clock.

overnight is designed before it's made again, by the best practices of software design and test design, with an architecture first where they take one, and the user doesn't review the design, as the purpose is already given, as the user said 「なんで私が見るの？ 目的は伝えてるよね？ ソフトウェア設計やテスト設計を使ってさきに設計したらいいだけでしょ？ それに先立ってアーキテクチャが必要ならそれも BP見てないの？」.

overnight's design follows the order that its best practices' inputs make, each made from the ones before: a product vision at dev/overnight/product-vision.md from the run's outcome and needs, which the README and the architecture take; the README; an architecture at dev/overnight/architecture.md, whose Sequences settle each kind of failure a work meets and whose Directory structure and Test strategy settle the split between bin/overnight and the Python code and how it's tested; the skeleton of plugins/overnight, its command's entry included; the unit cases in dev/overnight/tests, as test-design, since test-implementation is for tests that run the product whole; and then the code's bodies in plugins/overnight/scripts, since a maintainer finds each behavior traced to the design, and the error handling, the split, and the tests, each settled only after an evaluator's finding, now come from the design.

steps.settles: rnから夜に別プロセスのバッチを始め、キューの作業を指定した並行数で動かし、使用量の上限で止まった作業は間隔を伸ばしながら再開を試し、上限が解けたら止まったところから続き、朝には何が止まり何が再開したかが記録に残る。
